claims.text: Partial routing gives a frontier lead model delegation guidance compiled from profiled solo traces, and the lead chooses when and what to delegate at run time, with no model training.
At delta 0.75, partial routing raises the lead's ViBench score and lowers its cost, and raises its Terminal-Bench pass rate at about the same cost.
Task-level routers, including a hindsight oracle, score lower than partial routing on ViBench and cost more.
Unguided delegation to a cheaper worker improves results on ViBench but not on Terminal-Bench; adding the profiled guidance gives a further gain on both.
Giving the lead only the profiled subtask plan, with no worker, cuts cost on both benchmarks at a similar or higher score.
The LLM-judged subtask profile is stable across repeated judge runs, and the tiers are reproduced.
Profiling is cheap compared with training an orchestrator.
A single run with a second model pair on each benchmark suggests the gains carry over beyond the main pairs.

limits_authors.text: The main results use one model pair per benchmark and few tasks and runs.
It is untested whether the gains hold for pairs with smaller capability or price gaps.
The settings rho, tau and the number of profiling tasks were fixed, and their sensitivity is unknown.
The LLM annotator and judge were not validated against human labels.
The authors did not check whether the lead actually followed its tiers.
Delegation trades wall-clock time for cost.
Only coding and command-line workloads were evaluated.
The second-pair runs are not a full evaluation and are not meant to show that the method helps every pair.

likely_overclaims: The headline Terminal-Bench gain over the hindsight oracle and over the plan-only lead amounts to about one task out of 23, averaged over two runs. It may be within noise, yet it is described as the most of any method.
The ViBench gains depend strongly on delta. At low delta, partial routing scores below the lead alone and below unguided delegation on held-out apps, so the method helps only if delta is tuned well.
The guided arms score much higher on the profiling applications than on held-out ones, which suggests the profile partly overfits. The held-out margin over unguided delegation is modest.
The context-management explanation for the worker gain is a hypothesis, not tested.
Calling the delegation 'informed' assumes the lead follows its tiers, which the authors did not verify.
There is a potential conflict of interest: ViBench comes from Replit traces, and the paper discloses that Replit is a portfolio company of the authors' firm.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Partial routing. Offline, the lead and the worker each do the same tasks alone, and an LLM annotator then tags each step of their rollouts (gray) with a recurring subtask from a set \mathcal{S}; an LLM judge scores both models on each subtask, and \delta turns quality and cost saving into delegation tiers.
Figure 2: Cost and quality on the ten held-out ViBench applications, mean of three runs.
Figure 3: Cost and pass rate on the 23 held-out Terminal-Bench tasks, mean of two runs per task.

change_for_agents: If you already have subagent delegation and logged traces, profiling past solo runs of your lead and worker models into per-subtask delegate/conditional/keep tiers in the lead's prompt is a cheap, training-free way to cut cost and possibly raise quality. Sweep delta on a validation set, and expect delegation to take longer in wall-clock time.

compact.claim: Guiding a frontier lead model to delegate subtasks to a cheaper worker, using tiers profiled from past solo traces, beats both the lead alone and task-level routing on long coding tasks, without any training.
compact.method: An LLM annotator labels steps of lead and worker solo rollouts with recurring subtasks, and an LLM judge scores each model per subtask. Cost savings and quality risk are combined with a parameter delta into delegate/conditional/keep tiers, which go into the lead's prompt alongside a delegation tool.

results.finding: At delta=0.75 on held-out ViBench, the score rises from 70.2 to 78.5 at 19% lower cost.
On Terminal-Bench, the pass rate is 60.9% against 54.3% for the lead alone and for unguided delegation.
The hindsight oracle reaches at most 71.0 and Jev 60.5 on ViBench, both at higher cost.
The plan alone, with no worker, cuts cost by 39% on ViBench and 16% on Terminal-Bench.
Judge re-runs have an intraclass correlation of 0.97.

compact.limits: Only one main model pair per benchmark was tested, on few held-out tasks and runs; the LLM annotator and judge were not validated against human labels; and the fixed hyperparameters were not swept.
